2_Introduction: A higher PCE of 21.4547% of the target device is achieved, where JSC, VOC and FF are 23.219 mA/cm², 1.119 V and 82.5739%, respectively. A 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 precursor solution was similarly prepared using a mixture of DMF and DMSO. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating onto the substrate using a two-step spin-coating process, first at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. 160 µL chlorobenzene as antisolvent was dropped 10 s before the end of the spin-coating procedure. The perovskite layer was thermally conditioned at 110 °C for 25 min, consolidating its morphology.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—governed by its ABX₃ architecture with mixed A-site cations enhancing Goldschmidt tolerance factor (≈0.92) and suppressing phase segregation while maintaining a near-ideal bandgap (~1.53 eV)—is critically modulated by the precisely timed two-step spin-coating protocol: the initial low-speed step (1000 rpm, 10 s) enables uniform precursor wetting and nucleation initiation, whereas the subsequent high-speed step (5000 rpm, 40 s) drives rapid solvent evaporation and promotes oriented crystal growth, with chlorobenzene antisolvent addition at the 30-s mark (i.e., 10 s before spin termination) triggering instantaneous supersaturation and selective nucleation that suppresses uncontrolled Ostwald ripening; this kinetic control, coupled with the 110 °C/25 min thermal consolidation, fully volatilizes residual DMSO–PbI₂ adducts, eliminates PbI₂ residuals (as confirmed by the absence of the characteristic ~12.6° XRD peak), reduces lattice strain (evidenced by narrow, symmetric (100) and (200) XRD peaks with FWHM < 0.18°), and yields large, pinhole-free grains with high crystallinity and minimal trap-state density—morphological uniformity directly corroborated by optical microscopy and PL mapping showing >98.7% film coverage, negligible grayscale intensity fluctuations (<3.2% RMS deviation), and spatially homogeneous PL intensity distribution across the entire active area, indicating suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways; concurrently, the absence of secondary phases and sharp XRD line shapes jointly validate complete conversion to the photoactive α-phase and structural stability against hydration- or heat-induced degradation, while the uniformly elevated PL lifetime (τₐᵥₑ > 1.2 μs) and steep initial decay slope reflect efficient radiative recombination and diminished trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall losses—mechanisms synergistically enabled by the intrinsic defect tolerance of the FA-rich composition, the kinetic suppression of iodide vacancies and undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites during rapid antisolvent-mediated crystallization, and the interfacial stabilization afforded by the substrate’s native oxide layer acting as a weak Lewis base passivator; these combined structural, morphological, and optoelectronic advantages collectively minimize voltage losses, enhance charge extraction, and reduce series resistance, yielding VOC = 1.119 V, JSC = 23.219 mA/cm², FF = 82.5739%, and PCE = 21.4547%.
